title: Enterprise batch intake runbook for CS→PM handovers and rapid first-pass scoping
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create and validate a lightweight runbook + template bundle that Customer Success (CS) can use to batch enterprise feature asks and hand them to Product for a rapid first-pass evaluation. The goal is to reduce back-and-forth, standardize initial scoping (business value / implementation complexity / compliance surface), and produce a prioritized short-list that can be scheduled for deeper discovery. This ticket covers: 1) a cadence for weekly batch intake, 2) a fillable CS intake template, 3) an automated scoring heuristic for first-pass prioritization, and 4) guidance for required artifacts for in-depth scoping (security, data residency, SSO, cost targets).
acceptance_criteria: A reusable CS intake template exists and is published in Confluence/Drive
A 1-page runbook describing weekly batch cadence, reviewers, and decision criteria is published
An initial scoring heuristic (value, usage, customer tier, technical risk) implemented as a simple spreadsheet and example run for 20 queued asks
CS can prepare a batch using the template in under 60 minutes for up to 20 asks
PM can convert the top 5 scored asks into discovery tickets with clear next-step owners within 3 business days

notes: Scope decision: this flow handles non-bug, non-incident feature asks only. Bugs should continue to use support/bug triage channel.
Tradeoff: Spreadsheet + Zapier is faster to deploy but fragile for scale; build Console native intake if pilot shows >150 asks/month.
Risk: requests that touch 'private deployment' (on-prem/VPC) will create high compliance burden; include an explicit funnel step to route to Enterprise Success and Solutions Engineering.
Metric suggestions: time from CS submission to PM first-pass decision, % of batch converted to discovery, mean score of converted items, and cycle time to production for accepted asks.
